alignments.note: Interrogative he takes the fronted auxiliary (rule 17: 'Shall I not visit' gives Shall to the particle). The ASV rewrites the question auxiliary at the head of the parallel colon (Doth), which the Hebrew leaves under the one particle's scope with no conjunction; rule 25 gives every such occurrence to the one morpheme's discontinuous unit, headed on the first. Competing reading: Doth to the verb גָּמַר under rule 17's first sentence, since no interrogative morpheme stands in that colon.

אָפֵס 'come to an end' rendered by the fixed English 'clean gone'; kept whole as one rendering, headed on gone which carries the lexeme. Competing reading: clean as a supplied degree word, added under rule 44's surplus-particle test.
ASV writes a word for the preposition and one for the noun, so rule 2 splits rather than rule 40 fusing.
Suffix takes the possessive under rule 18.
Verb keeps the lexical verb; the fronted Doth is the interrogative particle's distributed occurrence (see s001).
No suffix on אֹמֶר; the supplied possessive is added under rule 18's closing sentence. The suffix of חַסְדּוֹ already holds its own his and is not a home for a second.
לְ → for, written separately from the noun's rendering.

דֹר וָדֹר rendered by the single adverb evermore, which carries the whole repetition and spends nothing on either occurrence; rule 22's first limit fuses the three morphemes under rule 30, headed on the first noun.

review_notes: Interrogative he read as distributed over both cola (Is ... Doth) under rule 25; alternative gives Doth to גָּמַר.
דֹר וָדֹר → evermore fused as one unit under rule 22/30.
